lessons.title: Common Phrasal Verbs: Meanings and Examples
lessons.content: Phrasal verbs are combinations of a verb and a preposition or adverb that create a meaning different from the original verb. Here are 25 common phrasal verbs with their meanings and examples.

details.explanation: To yield or give in to pressure or demands.
details.example: The company president finally bowed to pressure and resigned. / The government had to bow to public pressure. / I can't agree with you but I bow to your greater experience and knowledge.
details.burmese: အလျော့ပေးရသည်၊ လက်လွှတ်ရသည်။

details.explanation: To stop working (of a machine), or to deteriorate (of health or a situation).
details.example: Her health broke down under the pressure of work. / The machine must break down at this busy hour. / His van broke down.
details.burmese: (စက်)ပျက်သည်။ (ကိစ္စမရှိတဲ့အခြေအနေ)ယိုယွင်းသည်။

details.explanation: To appeal to or ask someone to do something; to visit someone.
details.example: The human rights group has called on the US to end the death penalty. / We sometimes have to call on outside expertise. / The President paid a courtesy call on Emperor Akihito.
details.burmese: ပန်ကြားသည်၊ အမှတ်ရပ်ခံသည်။

details.explanation: To become close friends with someone.
details.example: She chummed up with some girls from Bristol on holiday. / They chummed up in a short time. / It's good to see your children chumming up with mine so well.
details.burmese: အပြင်းအသင်းဖြစ်သည်။

details.explanation: To draw a line through a word or words to show they are wrong or not needed.
details.example: He could cross out half the words because they were unnecessary. / Two sentences were crossed out. / He crossed out three wrong words.
details.burmese: စာလုံး မကျက် ခြစ်ပစ်သည်။

details.explanation: To look through something quickly, browsing casually.
details.example: In bookshop, I picked up a novel by a new writer and began to flick through it. / I had a quick flick through your report. / I had a flick through the catalogue while I was waiting.
details.burmese: လှန်လှန်ကြည့်သည်။

details.explanation: To understand, solve, or calculate something.
details.example: I couldn't figure out what the teacher was talking about. / Please figure out the total cost. / We must figure out how to solve the problem.
details.burmese: သဘောပေါက်သည်၊ နားလည်သည်၊ တွက်ချက်သည်။

details.explanation: To choose something or try to achieve something.
details.example: I think I'll go for the steak. What are you having? / I think I will go for the fruit salad. / She is going for the world record in the high jump.
details.burmese: ရွေးချယ်သည်၊ ရယူရန် ကြိုးစားသည်။

details.explanation: To chase or pursue someone or something.
details.example: He went after the burglars. / Go after him and apologize. / He goes after every woman he meets.
details.burmese: လိုက်သည်။

details.explanation: To get revenge on someone for something they did.
details.example: She was trying to get back at him for humiliating her. / I will get back at him one day. / He will get back at you for this.
details.burmese: ကလည်စေချင်သည်။

details.explanation: To submit or give something to someone in authority.
details.example: I need to hand in my homework tomorrow. / Please hand in the document to me. / We handed in a letter of protest.
details.burmese: တင်သပ်သည်၊ အပ်အပ်သည်၊ အပ်နှံသည်။

details.explanation: To depend on something for its success or outcome.
details.example: My decision will hinge on your views. / The answers hinge on supply and demand. / But elections hinge on shorter-term concerns.
details.burmese: တည်သည်။

details.explanation: To think about something in the past.
details.example: Stop spending your time looking back. Live your life now and enjoy every moment! / Adults often look back on their childhood as a golden age. / When I look back I can see where we went wrong.
details.burmese: ပြန်လည်တူးဆွဲကြည့်သည်။

details.explanation: To take care of someone or something.
details.example: We look after the neighbours' cat while they are away. / I will look after her child when she is on a business trip. / It is a tradition that the young look after the old in their family.

details.explanation: To go around a place and look at things.
details.example: Let's look round this museum slowly. I think it will be interesting. / Let's look round the town this afternoon. / Have a look round the shop.
details.burmese: လှည့်ပတ်ကြည့်သည်။

details.explanation: To consider someone as being inferior or less important.
details.example: She looks down on anyone who hasn't had a university education. / You should never look down on poor people. / Never look down on yourself.
details.burmese: အထင်အမြင်သေးသည်။

details.explanation: To feel excited and pleased about something that is going to happen.
details.example: We look forward to hearing from you soon. / I always look forward to getting home to my wife and children. / I look forward to seeing you again.

details.explanation: To demolish or destroy a building.
details.example: The old warehouse has been pulled down. / It is easier to pull down than build. / The house was pulled down and the site redeveloped.
details.burmese: ဖျက်ချသည်။

details.explanation: To continue reading.
details.example: Please read on to the end of the chapter. / I took a book with me to read on the train. / If you like a good story, read on.
details.burmese: ဆက်ဖတ်သည်။

details.explanation: To read something aloud to others.
details.example: He began to read out loud. / She read out the letters to all of us. / He read out the names of all the winners.
details.burmese: ဖတ်ပြသည်။

details.explanation: To give a brief summary of something.
details.example: I can't sum up his whole philosophy in one sentence. / To sum up, there are three main ways of tackling the problem... / You have only 100 words in which to sum up his speech.
details.burmese: အကျဉ်းချုပ်သည်။

details.explanation: To improve or develop in a satisfactory way.
details.example: I have been told that if I don't shape up, I will lose my job. / He will shape up into an excellent basketball player. / Mark didn't shape up until he was thirty years old.
details.burmese: တိုးတက်အားကောင်းစေသည်။

details.explanation: To scold or reprimand someone.
details.example: The pupil was told off for being careless. / My parents told me off for coming home late. / They were told off to clean the latrines.
details.burmese: ဆူသည်၊ ကန့်သတ်သည်။

details.explanation: To gradually disappear or diminish.
details.example: The pain is slowly wearing off. / The effects of the drug were wearing off. / After the effectiveness of the vaccines wears off, the risk of actual infection returns.
details.burmese: တဖြည်းဖြည်းချင် ပျက်ပြယ်သွားသည်။

details.explanation: To completely destroy or eliminate something.
details.example: The government is trying to wipe out drug trafficking. / One dose of penicillin can wipe out the infection. / The plague once could wipe out a village.
details.burmese: ချမ်းနှိမ်သည်၊ တိုက်ဖျက်သည်။
